references.text: Jesus says that a disciple is not above his teacher, nor a servant above his master. It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher. This is a direct parallel to Luke 6:40 with nearly identical wording.
Jesus says that a servant is not greater than his master, nor an envoy greater than the one who sent him. The same principle regarding the relationship between master and disciple.
Jesus reminds the disciples that a servant is not greater than his master, linking this to persecution—they will be treated as their master was treated.
The disciple is called to follow Jesus' example by taking up his cross and following him—an extension of the idea that the disciple should become like his master.
Christ will transform our bodies and make them like his glorious body—an eschatological fulfillment of the promise that the fully trained disciple will be like his teacher.
Believers are predestined to be conformed to the image of God's Son—the goal of discipleship is to become like Christ, the master.
When Christ appears, we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is. This connects to the promise that the fully trained disciple will be like his teacher.

The ministry of the church aims to build up believers until they reach unity in faith and knowledge of God's Son, to mature manhood and the full measure of Christ's stature—to become fully trained like the master.
Paul works to present every person perfect (κατηρτισμένος/τέλειον) in Christ—the same idea of being fully equipped and made like the master.
